title: Sensitive Detection of Proteopathic Seeding Activity with FRET Flow Cytometry
protocol: Deep anesthetize a mouse with isoflurane (2%).
Perfuse the mouse with ice-cold PBS containing 0.03% heparin.
Extract the brain and place it in a cryo-vial.
Snap freeze the extracted tissue by placing it in liquid nitrogen.
Alternatively, freeze tissue on dry ice.
Transfer frozen tissue to -80 °C for storage if necessary.
Prepare homogenization buffer by dissolving protease inhibitors (EDTA free) into 1x TBS (1 tablet per 10 ml).
Vortex vigorously and store the buffer on ice.
Weigh frozen brain tissue in a disposable weigh boat.
Transfer the weighed tissue to a 5 ml conical tube.
Add ice-cold homogenization buffer to achieve a final solution concentration of 10% weight/volume.
Store the tube on ice temporarily.
Set the probe sonicator power to 20%, corresponding to approximately 75 W.
Adjust the pulser to 30%, corresponding to approximately 500 msec in pulse mode.
Clean the tip of the probe sonicator by rinsing with water, isopropanol, and then water again.
Wipe off the probe thoroughly between each solution rinse.
Submerge the clean probe into the homogenization buffer containing tissue.
Start the sonicator and deliver 25 total pulses using the set power and pulser settings.
Ensure that tissue is completely in suspension after sonication.
Be careful to avoid foaming of the sample during sonication.
Store homogenates on ice until all samples have been processed.
Spin homogenates at 21,300 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to a clean tube, taking care not to disturb the pellet.
Discard the pellet.
Aliquot the supernatant and store lysates at -80 °C.
In a sterile environment, aspirate culture medium.
Rinse cells with warm PBS and aspirate.
Trypsinize cells (3 ml of trypsin-EDTA (0.05%)) for 3 min.
Quench with warm culture medium (9 ml of DMEM, 10% FBS, 1% pen/strep, 1% GlutaMax).
Transfer cells to a conical tube immediately after quenching.
Centrifuge cells at 1,000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate medium and resuspend cell pellet in warm culture medium.
Determine the cell density using a hemocytometer for each cell line.
Resuspend cells harvested from a 10 cm dish at 90% confluency in 10 ml media to achieve approximately 1 million cells/ml.
Make a master mix of cells + media such that each well of a 96-well plate will contain 35,000 cells in 130 μl media for cell treatment ~18 hr after plating.
Using a multi-channel pipet, slowly pipette 130 μl of master mix cell suspension into each well of a flat bottom, tissue culture-treated 96 well plate.
Place the pipet tip in the center of the well without touching the bottom of the plate.
Allow the cells to settle by leaving the plate undisturbed for 10 min at RT.
Incubate O/N at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and ≥80% relative humidity.
When tau biosensor cells are 60-65% confluent, prepare seed transduction complexes as follows.
In one tube, combine transfection reagent with reduced-serum media to make a master mix.
Per well, add 1.25 μl transfection reagent and 8.75 μl reduced-serum media.
Flick the tube gently to mix.
Briefly spin down the tube.
Incubate for 5 min at RT.
In another tube, combine seed material with reduced-serum media.
Combine contents from the two tubes described, flick gently to mix, briefly spin down (1,000 x g, 5 sec), and incubate at RT for at least 20 min and up to 2 hr.
Gently pipette 20 μl of transduction complex on the side of individual biosensor wells.
Return treated cells to the incubator for 24-48 hr.
Incubate under the same conditions as described in step 3.6.
Harvest cells for FRET flow cytometry.
Aspirate all cell medium using a multi-channel pipette (150 μl per well).
Trypsinize cells for 5 min (50 μl).
Quench trypsinization with 150 μl chilled culture medium.
Transfer cells to a 96 well round bottom plate and centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate and discard the medium, being careful not to disturb the cell pellet.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 50 μl of 2% paraformaldehyde.
Incubate cells with paraformaldehyde for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge cells again at 1,000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate and discard paraformaldehyde solution carefully.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μl chilled flow cytometry buffer (HBSS with 1% FBS and 1 mM EDTA).
Run the plate immediately to avoid cell clumping.
Use a flow cytometer equipped with FRET-compatible laser lines and filter sets.
Click the well of interest using the software’s 96 well template.
Begin sample uptake and flow by clicking “play”.
Make plots or statistics tables by clicking the 'new analysis window' icon.
Change axis parameters on individual bivariate plots by clicking the title on either the X or Y axis and selecting the appropriate filter.
Shift cell populations or fluorescence signals by increasing or decreasing the voltages associated with the appropriate filters.
Run less than 1,000 events/sec to ensure accurate single-cell monitoring.
Make a Side Scatter-Area (SSC-A) vs Forward Scatter-Area (FSC-A) bivariate plot.
Adjust SSC and FSC voltages until the cell population is in the lower left quadrant.
Define the cell population by clicking the polygon tool (Gate P1).
Make a FSC-H vs FSC-A bivariate plot.
Apply Gate P1 to the bivariate plot by clicking “live” and selecting P1.
Click the polygon tool and define single cells (Gate P2).
Create 3 histogram plots for CFP, YFP, and FRET filters.
Apply Gate P2 to all histogram plots by clicking “live” and selecting P2.
Adjust voltages such that the median cell population in the CFP, YFP, and FRET histograms are between 0 and 1.
Excite cells with a 405 nm laser for CFP and FRET measurements.
Capture fluorescence with a 450/50 nm filter for CFP measurement.
Capture fluorescence with a 525/50 nm filter for FRET measurement.
Excite cells with a 488 nm laser for YFP measurement.
Capture fluorescence with a 525/50 nm filter for YFP measurement.
Perform compensation for CFP spillover into the FRET and YFP channels.
Spike in 30 µl of cell line #1 suspension into 200 µl of cell line #2 suspension immediately prior to compensating.
Click the “Instrument Settings” icon.
Select the 'compensation' tab and check 'matrix' to open the compensation table.
Make a FRET-A vs CFP-A bivariate plot, and apply gate P2 as described in step 6.3.
With cell lines 1+2 running, click the 'quadrant' icon and draw quadrants such that the fluorescence-negative and -positive populations are separated by the lower two quadrants (Gates LL3 and LR3).
Create a statistics table that displays the median fluorescence intensity (MFI) of FRET for the LL3 and LR3 gates.
Adjust the FRET parameter in the compensation matrix until the MFI of the FRET signal is equivalent between LL3 and LR3.
Make a YFP-A vs CFP-A bivariate plot, and apply gate P2 as described in step 6.3.
Draw quadrants (LL4 and LR4) similar to that done in step 6.4.3.
Create a statistics table that displays the MFI of YFP for LL4 and LR4.
Adjust the YFP parameter in the compensation matrix until the MFI of the YFP signal is equivalent between LL4 and LR4.
Highlight wells of interest after gate setup and compensation.
Run the remainder of the plate.
Export data files by clicking 'file', then 'copy'.
Select the 'data files' tab, highlight the experiment folder, and click 'copy'.
Change axis parameters on individual bivariate plots as needed.
Open FCS files in the flow cytometry analysis program.
Use a polygonal gate to define the cell population (SSC vs FSC) from cells treated with empty liposomes.
Define the singlet population (FSC-H vs FSC-A) from cells treated with empty liposomes.
Create a FRET vs YFP bivariate plot.
Draw a false FRET gate along the slope of the FRET-positive cell population to exclude YFP single-positive cells.
Plot empty liposome-treated CFP/YFP cells on a FRET vs CFP bivariate plot.
Introduce a polygonal gate along the slope of the population that extends upward and leftward away from the population.
